presets.title: Task share by country
presets.description: Exposure is not job loss. The original axis and full-sample reference averages stay fixed when countries are selected.

inputs.metric: Share of tasks at exposure levels 2 or 3, labelled under that country's conditions (the paper's 'economically exposed share')
inputs.method: Quoted from the paper: 'the economically exposed share means the share of tasks at levels 2 or 3'. Tasks are relabelled per country by their classification pipeline; the task universe is the same size for every country.
inputs.source: Garg, Crosta and Baier, Global Automation Atlas (2026), country panel from the replication repository
inputs.note: Not employment-weighted and not a share of jobs: the denominator is a common task universe, so variation across countries reflects country-conditioned labelling, not the size of each country's exposed workforce.
